data.title: Technical View: Cooling momentum signals further consolidation in Nifty 50; 25,300 key support for next week, Bank Nifty must hold 62,500
data.description:
NIfty outlook for November 30, 2026
  • Weakness below 25,500 and 25,300 would be required for bears to take control
  • Otherwise, the broader market structure remains favourable for the bulls
  • On the upside, 25,800 and 26,000 remain crucial resistance levels
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

The Nifty 50 witnessed a correction throughout the session on November 27 after gaining for a couple of sessions, falling over 1 percent. However, the index continued to trade within Monday's wide range of 25,300–26,000 for the third consecutive session.

The weakness appears to be part of a consolidation phase at higher levels and a cooling-off in momentum following the recent strong rally of around 17 percent. Consistent weakness and a decisive breakdown below the 25,500 and 25,300 support levels would be required for bears to take control. Otherwise, the broader market structure remains favourable for the bulls, with the index sustaining above all key moving averages. The short- and medium-term moving averages also continue to remain above the long-term moving averages.

On the upside, 25,800 and 26,000 remain crucial resistance levels. A decisive move above these hurdles could pave the way for a rally towards the record high zone of 26,350–26,400, according to market experts.

Momentum indicators point towards further consolidation and a weakening of bullish momentum. The RSI declined from overbought territory to 65.47 and remained below its signal line. However, it continued to hold above the 60 mark, keeping the broader momentum in the bullish zone.

The MACD remained above its signal line, indicating that the underlying trend strength is still intact. However, it continued to slope downwards towards the signal line, with the green histogram bar contracting for the 13th consecutive session. Together, these indicators suggest that bullish momentum is gradually losing strength, increasing the likelihood of further consolidation.

Related Stories

  • Taking Stock: Market snaps 4-week rally; Nifty below 25,650, Sensex sheds 989 pts
  • Black Friday: Sensex settles 1,000 pts lower, Nifty ends near 25,600; 5 key factors behind market cr...
  • Sensex, Nifty Near 10-Month High | US futures tick higher | Brent crude tops $96 | Opening Bell

According to Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities, the considerable gap between the spot price and short-term moving averages leaves room for further consolidation and intermittent profit booking.

The Nifty 50 opened lower and, after initial volatility, remained under pressure for most of the session. The index declined 277 points, or 1.07 percent, to close at 25,607. On the daily charts, it formed a long bearish candle with minor upper and lower shadows, highlighting selling pressure at higher levels.

However, "the overall bullish chart pattern remains intact and present weakness could be an opportunity to create longs at the lows. Bullish chart pattern like higher tops and bottoms is unfolding on the intraday timeframe chart and current weakness is likely to form a new higher bottom of the pattern," said Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities.

On the weekly chart, the Nifty formed a reasonable bearish candle near the highs after a stellar four-week rally, declining 0.75 percent. This indicates consolidation at higher levels. Despite trading close to its record highs, there are no significant signs of a reversal pattern emerging near the resistance zone, Nagaraj said.

According to him, the short-term correction is likely to end by next week. The immediate support to watch is around 25,300, while the crucial overhead resistance is placed at 26,000.

The weekly options data also point to 26,000 as a crucial resistance level, with the highest Call open interest concentrated at this strike. The 25,800 strike, which has the next-highest Call open interest, is likely to act as an immediate hurdle.

On the downside, the 25,500 strike, which has the next-highest Put open interest, is likely to provide immediate support. The 25,000 strike, with the highest Put open interest, remains a crucial support level for the index.

Meanwhile, India VIX, the market's fear gauge, declined another 1.72 percent to 16.55. However, it remained elevated and would need to move towards the 14 zone for volatility to ease meaningfully and market stability to improve. Until then, volatility is expected to remain high, warranting caution among market participants.

Bank Nifty

The banking index remained under pressure for the second consecutive session amid profit booking, ending 0.78 percent lower. It formed a small-bodied bearish candle with an upper wick, highlighting selling interest at higher levels.

Bank Nifty witnessed a decline of 890 points from the day's high, reflecting strong supply at elevated levels. However, it continued to trade within Monday's wide range of 62,500–65,200 for the third consecutive session.

The broader positional structure remains bullish, with the recent weakness appearing to be a cooling-off phase following the strong rally.

The RSI continued to decline from overbought territory but remained in the bullish zone at 66.01. The ADX remained elevated, supporting the underlying trend strength. The MACD also remained comfortably above its signal line despite sloping slightly downwards, while the green histogram bar contracted for the fourth consecutive session.

On the weekly chart, Bank Nifty declined 2.47 percent and formed a long bearish candle, indicating profit booking following a four-week rally that had taken the index to a record high.

"The significant gap between spot levels and short-term EMAs suggests scope for further consolidation and a moderation in momentum. The 62,400–62,500 zone is expected to act as immediate support. A sustained breakdown below this range could intensify profit booking towards 62,000," said Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities.

On the upside, the 63,500–63,600 zone remains the immediate resistance area, he added.

data.title: SEBI clarifies 65-year age limit for MII managing directors remains unchanged
data.description:
• SEBI clarifies MD age limit remains 65 years.
  • Proposed reducing single MII tenure to eight years.
  • Cumulative tenure across MIIs capped at 12 years.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Friday clarified that its November 20 consultation paper on strengthening the governance of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) does not propose any change to the maximum age limit of 65 years for their managing directors (MDs).

The clarification follows media reports suggesting that SEBI was considering a change in the age limit for MII managing directors.

SEBI said consultation papers set out proposals only for provisions where changes are intended. Provisions for which no change is proposed are not included in the paper.

The maximum age limit of 65 years for MII MDs remains unchanged. The proposals in the consultation paper relate only to their term and tenure at a single MII and across different MIIs.

Also read: SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine issue

Related Stories

  • SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine...
  • Sensex, Nifty down 0.5% this week; Brent above $98, Rupee at 93/$ | Closing Bell
  • SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations

In the consultation paper, SEBI has proposed reducing the maximum tenure of an MD at a single MII from 10 years to eight years, while capping cumulative tenure across MIIs at 12 years, with a maximum of three terms. For MDs already in office when the proposed rules take effect, the regulator has suggested a cumulative tenure cap of 15 years across institutions, while allowing them to complete their ongoing terms.

The proposals aim to address concerns over concentration of authority, prolonged dependence on individual executives and key-man risk at market infrastructure institutions, which perform important regulatory functions.

SEBI also clarified that a Public Interest Director (PID), MD or Executive Director (ED) holding office on the date the proposed amendments come into effect would continue in office until the end of their ongoing term.

The consultation paper has been issued for public comments, and SEBI said decisions on the proposals would be taken only after the consultation process. Stakeholders can submit comments and suggestions through SEBI's website until December 11, 2026.

data.description:

  • Brands like Zara and H&M diverted orders to India and other hubs.

Shares of Gokaldas Exports, Sportking India, and other textile companies rose up to 8% as a report said global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs, including India, in the first half of November.

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs, including India, in the first half of November, three factory owners told Reuters.

The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing, Reuters reported.

Gokaldas Exports and Sporking are suppliers for H&M and ZARA, whose shares rose 8% each on November 27.

Related Stories

  • Textile stocks: Gokaldas Exports, Arvind, Kitex Garments fall as proposed US tariffs raise export co...
  • Gokaldas Exports Q2 results: Net profit soars 410% YoY to Rs 41 crore
  • Gokaldas Exports Q2 consolidated PAT jumps to Rs 41 crore

Other textile companies' stocks like Vardhman Textiles, Trident rose 2.4% and 3.9%, respectively.

India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, told Reuters that higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.

"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

data.title: SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group may examine issue
data.description:
• SEBI may review the Rs 2 lakh retail IPO limit.
  • Retail investors typically apply for just one lot.
  • A working group is set up to review regulations.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may examine whether the Rs 2 lakh threshold for retail investors in initial public offerings (IPOs) needs to be revised as part of a broader review of issuance regulations, a senior official said.

The Rs 2 lakh limit has remained unchanged for more than 25 years, but the regulator has so far seen little merit in revising it, given that retail investors typically apply for a single lot in an IPO, which often costs around Rs 15,000, said Jeevan Sonparote, Executive Director, SEBI.

Speaking at Moneycontrol FiDEX 2.0 in Mumbai, Sonparote said that even if the retail investor threshold were raised to Rs 5 lakh, it may not materially change the amount investors apply for in an IPO.

“The limit of Rs 2 lakh has been a very old limit. It's more than 25 years now. This limit has not been reviewed. There were various attempts made earlier to review this particular limit,” Sonparote said.

However, he said the regulator had found little justification for revising the threshold, as retail investors typically apply for one lot in an IPO, which may cost around Rs 15,000.

Related Stories

  • SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations
  • SEBI bars Le Lavoir, chairman and 13 others over alleged price manipulation, fund diversion, action ...
  • APL Apollo’s minority shareholders will 'foot the bill' in Tata Steel deal: IiAS suggests Sebi sho...

“So, even if today if somebody says that I want to invest in a retail category, he is doing only one lot and one lot may not be more than Rs 15,000. So, even if I were to increase this to, let's say, Rs 5 lakh, a retail investor will continue to apply at Rs 15,000,” he said.

Also read: Grey market premium is akin to betting, SEBI seeks to choke revenue incentives for such platforms

Sonparote said the treatment of investors during the allotment process would also remain unchanged, irrespective of whether the threshold was increased.

“There appears to be no such reason to review the limit. However, if there is some such thought process, we should definitely look at it,” he said.

SEBI has already constituted a working group to review the issuance regulations, and the retail investor threshold could be among the issues taken up by the panel, Sonparote said.

“I think you'll be aware that SEBI has already set up a working group on the review of the issuance regulations. One of the issues would definitely be whether to review this particular limit. That should be one of the issues that the committee or working group should visit,” he said.

Also read: SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility 

In October 2010, SEBI, under the chairmanship of CB Bhave, doubled the retail investor limit for IPO applications to Rs 2 lakh from the earlier cap of Rs 1 lakh, which had been in force since March 2005.

The issue has been raised several times by various stakeholders since then, but SEBI has held back from changing the limit, as IPO application data did not support the proposal.

US stock futures rallied sharply on Friday, signalling a strong opening for Wall Street as trading resumes after the Thanksgiving holiday, with renewed investor appetite for beaten-down artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. The gains come towards the end of a volatile week that saw dramatic swings in technology stocks amid persistent concerns over AI investments and elevated valuations.

Nasdaq 100 futures surged 729 points, or 2.8 percent, to 26,829.3, while S&P 500 futures advanced 144.8 points, or 2 percent, to 7,340.5. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 672 points, or 1.3 percent, to 50,900.

The rally in US stock futures gathered momentum during Asian trading, building on Wednesday's late-session recovery on Wall Street ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

AI stocks set for recovery after volatile week

US technology stocks have witnessed sharp swings this week as investors weigh increasingly attractive valuations following the recent correction against persistent concerns over the massive capital expenditure undertaken by AI companies and the potential returns on these investments.

Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive triggered a spectacular rally on Monday, with the chipmaker's shares surging 31.5 percent and restoring nearly $1 trillion in market capitalisation. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5 percent, while the S&P 500 gained 4.7 percent.

However, the recovery lost momentum over the following two sessions. Nvidia shares fell 5.9 percent on Tuesday and another 3.9 percent on Wednesday, while shares of Anthropic slipped below their IPO price of $83 apiece, less than a week after the Claude developer's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.

The Nasdaq Composite plunged more than 4 percent during Wednesday's session before recovering much of its losses to close 0.6 percent lower. The S&P 500 declined 0.3 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.3 percent.

Asian markets extend gains

The renewed appetite for technology stocks was also reflected in Asian equity markets, with the MSCI Asia Pacific Index advancing 1.8 percent on Friday. South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix was among the stocks leading the regional recovery for a second consecutive session.

Asian technology stocks have been particularly hard hit by the recent unwinding of the global AI trade, with semiconductor-heavy markets such as South Korea and Taiwan suffering steep losses this month.

US Fed rate hike expectations remain elevated; Brent nears $98

Despite the recovery in equities, expectations of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve remain firmly entrenched. Traders are pricing in a 99 percent probability of an interest rate increase at the US Fed's December meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch, Reuters reported.

Meanwhile, international crude oil prices reversed their morning losses amid persistent concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East. Brent crude advanced 1.3 percent to $97.8 a barrel, adding to its sharp gains this week.

Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) Ltd initial public offering (IPO) continues to see robust demand for the second day of its share sale in the primary market, led by retail investors and QIBs. The Rs 361-crore IPO was fully subscribed on the first day of bidding.

The issue has received bids for 1.44 crore 30 shares as against 1.04 crore shares on offer, as per NSE data, till 2 pm.

The category for retail investors was subscribed 4 times and the portion for Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) also received full subscription of 1.01 times. The quota for non-institutional investors was subscribed 50 per cent.

Earlier, it raised Rs 162.34 crore from anchor investors.

The IPO will conclude on November 30, with a price band of Rs 181-191 per share.

The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets.

A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services LLC, to fund the setting up of four new casual dining restaurants.

The funds will also be used for repayment or prepayment of outstanding borrowings and general corporate purposes.

Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) is a luxury food services business focused on providing curated culinary experiences. Its business model comprises event catering, casual dining restaurants, cloud kitchens and banquets and integrated food and beverage services.

The company operates several casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens under brands such as India Bistro, Art of Dum, China Bistro and Glocal in India and the United Arab Emirates.

In its events catering business, the company counts Hardcastle Restaurants, the master franchisee operator of McDonald's in western and southern India, Zee Entertainment and Greenply among its clients.

Foodlink is expected to debut on the stock market on December 3.
